items.title: William "Ba Ba" Ridgley Interview, 1959-06-02
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Can you tell me about, some more about Baptiste de Lille? I never got to know him. He died long before my time. ... [INTERVIEWEE] But this is what happened to him. He uh, went out of the audible mile. Oh I believe I heard that. And he stayed in Jacksonville about 14 or 15 years.

ctx.x: I was going to ask about the very first bands you remember playing, hearing, before you took up music. Did that, up in the country, were any of the New Orleans bands up there? John Robichaux. John Robichaux.

See, John Robichaux. And I heard them all because, you see, I worked at that grocery, and whenever they give dancers, every band had to pass that store to get where they was going to play in, in the little place back there most of them. And they all used to stop there and play at the stores, advertising there, you know. Yes. They'd stop there and play a couple of tunes, and we'd give them a couple of drinks, you see. And then they'd leave and they'd go. That's where they had to go. But the Robichaux band played…
Tucker. Tucker. It was the first slide. Slide trumpet player I had to sing.
